chose: build ONLY the neglect reading (commits-since-last-run) as a SessionStart section — not the unwired-input reading, not the gate-adoption reading
over: a three-reading 'coherence work is due' section covering neglect + unwired inputs + unadopted gates
because: re-measured all three after today's fixes, per BEFORE YOU ADD A CONCEPT COUNT ITS INSTANCES. NEGLECT has plural subjects on both repos: coherence economy 45 commits / drift 45 (mass 2, atlas 2, verify 1); hoist economy 28 / mass 11 / full-tier 9 (verify 1, atlas 1). UNWIRED INPUTS now has ZERO subjects: hoist .coherence/read-traces/ holds a2875153efa060fa7.jsonl (2733 bytes) and coherence holds one trace + one calibration sample, so the condition the reading would detect no longer exists anywhere — it was a one-shot config bug, fixed, and a detector for it would fire never. UNADOPTED GATES is not representable: coherence is 6-of-7 with contracts reasoned N/A, and there is no config key distinguishing 'not adopted' from 'reasoned not applicable', so on any consuming project it would fire permanently and non-actionably — the dilution the brief forbids. QUERY to re-run: for each status.json section, `git rev-list --count <section.commit>..HEAD`; for unwired inputs, `ls .coherence/read-traces`

chose: a section that has NEVER run is silent — only a section with a recorded run can be reported stale
over: reporting 'economy has never run' for absent status.json sections
because: an absent section is ambiguous three ways: never ran, does not record, or not applicable to this project. Reporting the first would fire permanently and non-actionably on every consuming project that has no reason to run drift or economy — dilution of the highest-traffic block, the one failure mode the brief names as fatal. It also collapses into the unadopted-gates reading I already declined for being unrepresentable. Neglect as defined is 'the tree moved while the instrument did not' — that presupposes the instrument moved once. Never-ran is unadoption, a different finding with no signal here

chose: append the due section at the hook's emit site, keeping agentInstructions() a pure clock-free function
because: agentInstructions is printed verbatim by `coherence hooks` (hooks.ts:310) and asserted byte-wise by test/conjecture.test.ts. Making it git-dependent would make `coherence hooks` output vary by repo state and by day — the exact hazard commands.ts documents at 'NO TIMESTAMP IN THE RENDERED BLOCK, on purpose … every normalization a freshness gate needs is a hole in that gate'. Composing at the emit site keeps the pure function pure and the impure reading isolated and separately testable

chose: baseline due.ts's two html-value sink rows rather than reword the emitted text
over: removing the `"<what you did not do>"` angle-bracket placeholders so the heuristic stops matching
because: lint-sinks' html-value heuristic fires on interpolation near angle brackets; due.ts:264 is TERMINAL PROSE handed to an agent's context, never rendered as HTML, and the identical construction in hooks.ts's agentInstructions is already baselined for the same reason (3 hooks.ts rows in public/sinks-baseline.json). Rewording to appease the heuristic would degrade the instruction — the placeholder convention is what the other three imperatives in the same block use — for zero safety

chose: 531 lines (2 files, 8 symbols) buys the run record a READER — the first thing that reads status.json's provenance stamps back
over: leaving the stamps unread and the neglect invisible
because: every section of .coherence/status.json has stamped its own commit since v0.10, and nothing ever asked whether those stamps were still current. Measured today: coherence economy 45 commits behind and drift 45; hoist economy 28 and mass 11. src/due.ts (307 lines) is the reading, test/due.test.ts (224) is 14 tests of which 8 are NEGATIVE — the property being bought is SILENCE on a current tree, because this text joins the SessionStart block that reaches every adopting project on repin. Growth is in Harness core (+307) and Executable contracts (+224), which is the ratio a mechanism whose main risk is firing too often should have
